### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.statusline

### Question

Hi, is it possible to modify the statusline to also include a clock perhaps with a `os.date("%R")`? Also, I wanted to understand why for some filetypes, I get N/C/V/I/R for the different modes, while for others I get the modes in complete words. (For example, for `mail` filetype, I get the modes in complete words, but not for `R`, `tex` or `luascript`, and perhaps for others too.) Just curious.

comment_data.body:
> ... is it possible to modify the statusline to also include a clock perhaps with a `os.date("%R")`?

Yes, it is possible by setting custom `config.content.active` to a function that uses `os.date("%R")` to create a section and uses it. I'd suggest starting with [this default function for active content](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4dd209e4f03bacd46d6d87408b2529a8823112fb/doc/mini-statusline.txt#L86-L107) and work from there.

> Also, I wanted to understand why for some filetypes, I get N/C/V/I/R for the different modes, while for others I get the modes in complete words.

It does not depend on filetype, but on the total width of the window. That content comes from [`section_mode()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4dd209e4f03bacd46d6d87408b2529a8823112fb/doc/mini-statusline.txt#L210): one letter is a short form and full word is a full form. Short form is shown if window's width is less than `trunc_width` argument (which in default active content [is 120](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4dd209e4f03bacd46d6d87408b2529a8823112fb/doc/mini-statusline.txt#L87)).

reply_data.body:
> Do I set it up as a function?

Yes, with something like this:

```lua
return {
  "echasnovski/mini.statusline",
  priority = 1000,
  config = function()
    local active = function()
      -- *This* is the place that gets adjusted
      local mode, mode_hl = MiniStatusline.section_mode({ trunc_width = 100 })
      local git           = MiniStatusline.section_git({ trunc_width = 40 })
      local diff          = MiniStatusline.section_diff({ trunc_width = 75 })
      local diagnostics   = MiniStatusline.section_diagnostics({ trunc_width = 75 })
      local lsp           = MiniStatusline.section_lsp({ trunc_width = 75 })
      local filename      = MiniStatusline.section_filename({ trunc_width = 140 })
      local fileinfo      = MiniStatusline.section_fileinfo({ trunc_width = 120 })
      local location      = MiniStatusline.section_location({ trunc_width = 75 })
      local search        = MiniStatusline.section_searchcount({ trunc_width = 75 })

      return MiniStatusline.combine_groups({
        { hl = mode_hl,                  strings = { mode } },
        { hl = 'MiniStatuslineDevinfo',  strings = { git, diff, diagnostics, lsp } },
        '%<', -- Mark general truncate point
        { hl = 'MiniStatuslineFilename', strings = { filename } },
        '%=', -- End left alignment
        { hl = 'MiniStatuslineFileinfo', strings = { fileinfo } },
        { hl = mode_hl,                  strings = { search, location } },
      })
    end

    require("mini.statusline").setup({
      content = { active = active },
      use_icons = false,
      set_vim_settings = false,
    })
  end,
}
```

I do understand that this is a lot of code for a small change, but this is by design: the amount of flexibility statusline needs to be "enough" for most of users is *very* high, so adjusting by writing custom function (however complex) is intentional.
